chapter: Heroin and the Miles Davis years
title: Miles on Sugar Hill and the square at 150th Street
summary: Miles hung out with Sugar Hill peers like Roy Haynes, Sonny Rollins and Gil Coggins in a little park.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Did he hang with the Sugar Hill gang, so to speak?

During a period, yeah. There was a period when Miles would come up on the Hill. But there were a lot of cats up there, his peers, for him to be around. Roy Haynes lived up that way. So it wouldn’t be strange to see Miles in the square where we used to hang out. He was close with Sonny. There would be a lot of people that would have a relationship with Miles in that area. Gilly Coggins was on the scene. He made the recordings that – I suggested that Miles get Gilly when he was looking for a piano player. There was Arthur Taylor, who Miles used from time to time, Kenny Drew, Walter Bishop. So we – that neighborhood . . .
The square was on 150th Street between St. Nicholas Place and St. Nicholas Avenue. It was just a little park right there. We used to sit on the benches in there.

Yeah, went out. Like when I left my house and I would be going out after dinner or something, I would – that’s where I would walk to, from 158th Street all the way down there to see if anybody’s in the square. Sometimes it would be nobody. Sometimes be a lot of cats in there.
